IMAGE 1 is the picture you edit: the lower part of a frame of our own rhythm game's play screen. In image 1 that panel is only a FLAT placeholder drawing (a blurred blue sky).

IMAGE 2 is a LOOK REFERENCE ONLY: a screenshot of the sky gear of another rhythm game. Take from it only the look of the panel at the bottom of its gear: a real daytime sky as a photograph shows it: deep clear azure at the top, towering bright white cumulus clouds lit by the sun with soft blue shadows, sunlight glowing low in it, and a few hairline curves of white light sweeping across like long-exposure trails, with a tiny sparkle where they meet the light. Do NOT copy anything else from image 2: not its layout, not its tall lane frame, not its stars, not its dashes, not its small readouts (the rings and the words over them), not its text, not the dotted meter at its right side.

Keep image 1's framing EXACTLY: the same camera, the same zoom, the same crop; your picture must overlay image 1 pixel for pixel, so the judge line, the dashed strip and the two side rails stay at exactly the same places and sizes. Do not zoom in, do not crop, do not widen, do not recompose, do not enlarge or shrink the panel, and do not move the picture toward image 2's composition. Repaint ONLY the panel: the area under the dashed strip, between the inner edges of the two side rails, down to the bottom edge of the image. Keep every other pixel exactly as it is: the lanes, the notes, the judge line and the flash on it, the dashed strip, the rails, the dark background.

The panel becomes ONE thick slab of clear glass lying flat like a console between the rails and seen exactly from this camera, as a photorealistic 3D render at the finish of a commercial console game, and sealed inside the glass is the sky of image 2: you look down through the glass into a real blue sky with white cumulus clouds at different depths under the surface (the nearer ones larger), sunlit, with soft blue shadows; a few hairline curves of white light sweep through it as in image 2. The glass's top surface carries a faint, soft reflection, and its top edge under the dashed strip is a bevelled lip catching the light. The slab stays inside the rails everywhere: nothing rises over the rails or above the strip, and it runs on down past the bottom edge of the image (no front edge is seen).

The slab is sky all over: NO windows, NO display, NO dark plates, NO insets, NO frames, NO sockets (the game shows its numbers elsewhere). The flat placeholder of image 1 only shows where the panel is; paint the sky anew.

Deliberately PLAIN and calm: NO wings, NO feathers, NO birds, NO round medallion or emblem, NO ornate frames, NO scrollwork, NO sun disc, NO lens flare rings, NO aeroplanes, NO rainbow. Deep blue lies right under the dashed strip and the first clouds begin a little below it: that upper part is what players see most, so the finest clouds and the curves of light are there; toward the bottom edge the clouds grow larger and calmer.

Colours as in image 2: azure and cobalt blue, bright white clouds with pale blue shadows, a little warm sunlight low in it.

One soft key light from the top-left. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, and nothing over the lanes.
